text:
Samir Bhat: heads up — since yesterday's runtime patch we're seeing p95 and p99 latency spikes on rdx-gpt-13b-v2 for hosted inference. Trend started ~ 09:12 UTC, affects multiple regions but highest in us-east1.
Samir Bhat: p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~480ms for short prompts (<128 tokens). p99 is 1.1s -> 3.6s. Error rates are unchanged, just tail latencies.
SRE Oncall Bot: alert: p99_latency > 2s (rdx-gpt-13b-v2) — triggered at 09:14 UTC.
Andy Support: we've got two paying customers on Dedicated opening tickets — they see timeouts on chat endpoints. They've sent request ids: req_0a1b2c, req_0a1b2d.
Marta Li: thanks Samir — any recent config/compile changes? I looked at the deploy notes: runtime v1.27.3 included a kernel selection change + enablement of FlashAttention by default for grouped-attn path.
Jiwoo Park: right — we flipped kernel-policy to 'pick-fastest' and bumped the NV attention-first compile flag. There's also a flag that prefers FlashAttention over SDPA when available.
Samir Bhat: repro (minimal): curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rdx-gpt-13b-v2","input":"hi"}' with header x-request-id:req_0a1b2c — observe single-token latency ~150ms earlier, now 600ms.
Samir Bhat: attaching flame traces (snippet):
```
cpu: 8%  | gpu: 72% | waiting_for_kernel_selector  ->  blocking on kernel load (200ms) -> kernel exec 400ms
callstack: runtime/kernel_selector::select -> kernel_launch -> attention_flash_wrapper -> fallback_sdpa
```
Jiwoo Park: interesting — stack shows kernel loader thrashing and fallback path showing up. Could be that the FlashAttention kernel is failing for certain sequence lengths and falling back to a slower SDPA path, or the kernel was compiled with different memcpy semantics causing stalls.
Marta Li: check /opt/runtime/kernels/active_manifest.json on a couple of nodes and the kernel checksum from the build job. The manifest should show preferred: flash_attn_v2 with backend_id: fa_v2_2026.
Samir Bhat: checked on host rdx-eu-01: manifest lists flash_attn_v2 but the binary timestamp is 2026-02-10 while build id is 2026-03-04. Mismatch.
Andy Support: customers are asking for ETA; can we do a temporary mitigation?
Jiwoo Park: quick mitigation options: 1) flip ATTENTION_PREFERENCE=sdpa in runtime config to force SDPA (more stable) 2) revert kernel-policy to 'legacy' so kernel selector doesn't try new flash kernels 3) hotfix to pin kernel binary to the tested checksum.
Marta Li: prefer minimal blast radius: set ATTENTION_PREFERENCE=sdpa for hosted pool and restart warm workers. That should drop p95 back but may increase GPU CPU usage slightly.
Samir Bhat: I ran a canary: set ATTENTION_PREFERENCE=sdpa on 10% of traffic in us-east1 — p95 dropped from 480ms -> 130ms on canary. Looks promising.
Deploy Bot: rollout change: feature flag ATTENTION_PREFERENCE=sdpa applied to pool hosted-us-east-1-canary at 09:32 UTC by Jiwoo Park.
SRE Oncall Bot: autoscale: added 10 extra warm workers to hosted-us-east-1-canary at 09:35 UTC.
Jiwoo Park: root cause hypothesis: build pipeline produced a non-deterministic FlashAttention binary variant (different compile flags -O3 vs -Ofast or different CUDA sm arch compile target) so selector attempted to use it, kernel load failed in some path, and fallback path has blocking behavior causing long tail.
Marta Li: immediate action plan: 1) widen canary to 50% by 09:50 if stable 2) concurrently validate kernel checksum across regions 3) disable 'pick-fastest' kernel-policy until we have deterministic artifacts 4) schedule rollback of v1.27.3 if mitigation fails.
Samir Bhat: repro steps for runtime team to reproduce locally:
1) checkout runtime@v1.27.3
2) build kernels with env: CUDA_SM=70, ATTENTION_IMPL=flash_attn
3) run micro-benchmark with seq_len distribution [16,32,64,128] and tighten concurrency to 32
4) check logs for fallback to sdpa and measure kernel load times
Command snippet:
```
make build-kernels && 
CUDA_SM=70 ATTENTION_IMPL=flash_attn ./runtime --bench --model rdx-gpt-13b-v2 --concurrency 32 --seq_dist "16:0.6,32:0.2,128:0.2"
```
Jiwoo Park: noted — also try forcing mismatched binary by altering kernel_id in manifest to simulate checksum mismatch; this reproduces the kernel-loader stall locally.
Andy Support: for customer comms: "We have identified an attention-kernel regression introduced in yesterday's runtime rollout. We have a mitigation and will continue to roll it out; no data loss. ETA for full remediation: 3 hours."
Marta Li: temporary live mitigation performed: ATTENTION_PREFERENCE=sdpa rolled to 50% at 09:48, 100% by 09:55 for hosted pools. After 100% switch p95 ~130ms, p99 ~240ms.
Samir Bhat: follow-ups: create postmortem and PR for deterministic kernel artifact tagging. Proposed short-term fix PR: pin kernel_policy to 'legacy' and add manifest checksum validation during startup that logs and rejects bad binaries (fast fail to prevent blocking fallback).
Jiwoo Park: longer-term: add a kernel compatibility test in CI that runs FlashAttention binary across seq lengths and ensures no fallback to SDPA and that kernel load time < 50ms. Also add fuzzy tests over compile flags (-Ofast vs -O3) and target archs.
Marta Li: assignables: Jiwoo -> PR for ATTENTION_PREFERENCE feature flag default and manifest checksum; Samir -> run synthetic p99 tests and collect traces; Andy -> customer comms update; SRE -> incident ticket and postmortem.
Deploy Bot: change summary: ATTENTION_PREFERENCE flag rollout completed at 09:55 UTC; runtime-pipeline v1.27.3 remains in place but with kernel-policy=legacy.
SRE Oncall Bot: incident created: INC-2026-042, severity P2 (tail latency), owner: eng-runtime oncall.
Samir Bhat: stack snippet to include in postmortem (example):
```
[09:14:02] kernel_loader::open("/opt/runtime/kernels/fa_v2_2026.bin") -> ENOENT
[09:14:02] kernel_selector: fallback to sdpa_impl
[09:14:02] sdpa_impl: acquire_mutex -> wait 200ms -> exec
```
Marta Li: next steps timeline: 1) stable mitigation done (now) 2) CI/kernel checks in 48h 3) postmortem doc with timelines and RCA in 72h 4) follow-up RFC on kernel-artifacting and signing.
Jiwoo Park: I'll open the kernel artifacting RFC and a prereq checklist for the builds.
Andy Support: I'll send update to affected customers and mark tickets with incident reference INC-2026-042.
Samir Bhat: thanks everyone. If anyone sees residual tail >500ms please ping here and include request ids. Will drop the final postmortem link here when ready.
Marta Li: adding runbook pointer: https://runbooks.redwood.ai/eng-runtime/attention-regressions — follow section 'fast mitigation' (flip ATTENTION_PREFERENCE).
SRE Oncall Bot: status: resolved -> mitigation applied, monitoring for regression windows next 12h.
